text: DSH Desktop Window Status Saving 是面向 Windows 桌面端的 DSH 插件，会在应用运行时记录主窗口的位置、尺寸和最大化状态，并在窗口首次显示前恢复。它通过 Win32 窗口接口跟踪窗口变化，将状态保存到 DSH home 的 JSON 文件；显示器布局变化时会将窗口放入可用工作区。适合希望重启后继续使用原窗口布局的桌面用户。可选设置 DSH_HOME 指定状态文件所在目录。

DSH Desktop Window Status Saving restores the main window's size, position, and maximized state on Windows. It saves changes in the DSH home directory and reapplies them on the next launch. If a display is unavailable, it fits the window into a work area. DSH_HOME selects the state file directory.
让 DSH Desktop 重启后还原主窗口的位置和大小
窗口每次启动都回到默认位置，能记住上次的布局吗？
Restore my DSH desktop window to the same position and size after restarting
DSH Desktop Window Status Saving 的功能「记忆窗口布局」：跟踪主窗口的位置、尺寸和最大化状态，并保存变化；下次启动时在窗口显示前恢复，显示器布局变化时适配到可用工作区。

**The DeepSeek Harness Desktop window, exactly where you left it.** Size, position and maximized state are saved while you use the app and restored before the window is painted — no flash back to the default 1280 × 820.

@jamolpe88/dsh-desktop-windowstatus-saving README · What it does：- Remembers the **size**, **position** and **maximized** state of the DeepSeek Harness main window.
- Applies the saved placement **while the window is still hidden**, so the window appears directly at its final geometry instead of resizing after it is visible.
- Detects changes while the app runs (drag, resize, snap, maximize) and saves them within a second.
- Saves a final value when DSH quits, including the quit-to-tray path and a normal window close.
- Keeps the maximized flag through **minimize** and tray hide: minimizing a maximized window and then quitting still reopens it maximized.
- Restores onto the display where the rectangle was saved, including displays at **negative coordinates** (left of or above the primary one).
- Moves and shrinks the window into the nearest work area when the saved display is gone.
- Writes the state atomically and only when it changed.

@jamolpe88/dsh-desktop-windowstatus-saving README · What it does not do：- It does not add UI, commands, tools or settings.
- It does not run a second process or a background service.
- It does not use window titles to identify the app.
- It does not touch windows of other applications.
- It does not restore fullscreen or minimized state (the window always opens visible).
- It does not persist per-profile or per-session geometry: one window, one saved place.

@jamolpe88/dsh-desktop-windowstatus-saving README · Install：From npm:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add @jamolpe88/dsh-desktop-windowstatus-saving
```

From the repository:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:JaMoLpE88/dsh-desktop-windowstatus-saving
```

From a local checkout, while developing:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add C:\path\to\dsh-desktop-windowstatus-saving
```

@jamolpe88/dsh-desktop-windowstatus-saving README · Install：Restart DeepSeek Harness Desktop after installing. The plugin only restores on startup, so a live install starts saving immediately but waits for the next launch to restore.

@jamolpe88/dsh-desktop-windowstatus-saving README · Usage：1. Move, resize or maximize the main window.
2. Close DSH normally, or quit from the tray.
3. Open DSH again: the window is already at the geometry you left, on the same display.

There is nothing to configure and no panel to open. To forget the saved window, delete the state file and restart.

@jamolpe88/dsh-desktop-windowstatus-saving README · Restore before the first frame：DSH Desktop creates its main `BrowserWindow` hidden at startup and shows it only after the plugin host is ready and the page has loaded. The plugin runs inside that host and finds the window while it is still hidden:

```
main window created (hidden, 1280 × 820)
   │
   ├── plugin host starts, plugin loads
   │      └── SetWindowPlacement(saved bounds, maximized)

@jamolpe88/dsh-desktop-windowstatus-saving README · Restore before the first frame：Because the placement is applied while the window is hidden, the usual visible jump from the default size is gone. The state file records this with `restore.whileHidden: true`.

@jamolpe88/dsh-desktop-windowstatus-saving README · Window identity：The plugin only acts on the product window: the top-level Chromium window (`Chrome_WidgetWin_1`) owned by the Electron process that launched the plugin host, with no owner window and a plausible size. It never matches on window titles — a browser tab called “DeepSeek Harness” is not a window of the app.

@jamolpe88/dsh-desktop-windowstatus-saving README · State file：- Writes are atomic (temporary file + rename), so a crash cannot leave a truncated document.
- The file is written only when the geometry or the maximized flag changes, and once more during shutdown.
- A corrupt file is ignored and replaced on the next save.
- A file written by a newer plugin version is left untouched.

@jamolpe88/dsh-desktop-windowstatus-saving README · Multi-monitor：The work area used to fit the window comes from the monitor of the saved rectangle, not from the monitor the window happens to be on at startup. Negative coordinates are valid and preserved. If the monitor is gone, the window moves into the nearest work area and shrinks to fit.

@jamolpe88/dsh-desktop-windowstatus-saving README · Compatibility：| | |
|---|---|
| DSH | `>= 0.2.1-rc.3` (the only version tested by the author) |
| Node | `>= 22` |
| OS | Windows 11 (tested); Windows 10 untested; macOS and Linux unsupported |
| Profile | `desktop` |
| Runtime | Host plugin, Win32 through the `koffi` copy included with DSH |
| Catalog | [listed on dsh-plugin.org](https://dsh-plugin.org/plugins/jamolpe88/dsh-desktop-windowstatus-saving) |

@jamolpe88/dsh-desktop-windowstatus-saving README · Compatibility：Validation status: **tested on Windows 11 with DSH Desktop 0.2.1-rc.3** (2026-10-26) across normal restarts, maximized restarts, maximize → minimize → quit, tray quit, and a two-display layout with negative coordinates. The state file reported `restore.whileHidden: true` after the restarts, and the saved geometry matched the live window.

Not validated: macOS, Linux, Windows 10, other DSH versions and the web profile.

@jamolpe88/dsh-desktop-windowstatus-saving README · Limits：- **Windows only.** The plugin calls `user32` through `koffi`; other platforms are skipped.
- **Physical pixels.** Changing display scaling keeps the physical size; it does not rescale to DIP.
- **Fullscreen is not restored.** Maximized is; fullscreen is not saved as a state.
- **Minimized is not restored.** The app always opens visible.
- **Snap groups are not recreated.** Windows 11 snap layouts are not part of the saved state.
- **One window.** Only the main product window is tracked.
- **If DSH ever persists geometry itself**, uninstall this plugin.

@jamolpe88/dsh-desktop-windowstatus-saving README · Privacy：- No network requests, no telemetry, no analytics.
- The plugin reads Win32 window state and writes one JSON file in the DSH home.
- It never reads window contents, titles, session data or credentials.
- It never changes windows of other applications.

See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for the short policy.

@jamolpe88/dsh-desktop-windowstatus-saving README · Troubleshooting：**The window still opens at 1280 × 820.**
Confirm the bundle is installed in the `desktop` profile and restart the app. A live install does not restore until the next launch. Also check that no other window-position plugin is enabled: two savers fight over the same window.

**The window flashes at the default size before moving.**
The plugin was not loaded before the window was shown. Check that the bundle is enabled and that DSH is the Desktop build, not the CLI or the web profile.

@jamolpe88/dsh-desktop-windowstatus-saving README · Troubleshooting：**I want to reset the saved window.**
Delete `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\window-bounds.json` and restart.

**A different monitor is gone.**
The saved rectangle no longer touches any display, so the window is moved into the nearest work area and fitted.

@jamolpe88/dsh-desktop-windowstatus-saving README · Development：```bash
npm install
npm test        # 20 tests: geometry, state machine, atomic store, Win32 bindings
npm run check   # syntax check for every module
```

The Win32 suite is a smoke test (struct sizes, `EnumWindows`, placement read); the real restore path is validated in the running Harness. The README illustrations are generated by `assets/src/render_assets.py` (Pillow, Windows fonts).

Local install:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add C:\path\to\dsh-desktop-windowstatus-saving
```

@jamolpe88/dsh-desktop-windowstatus-saving README · Third-party：The plugin uses the copy of [koffi](https://koffi.dev/) 3.1.1 (MIT, Niels Martignène) that ships with DeepSeek Harness Desktop, so installing this package does not build or download any native dependency. The repository keeps koffi as a dev dependency for the Win32 test suite.
